Ten grams ($10\text{ g}$) of an impure sample of sodium carbonate is added to $100\text{ cm}^3$ of a $0{,}2\text{ mol}\cdot\text{dm}^{-3}$ solution of hydrochloric acid. The acid is in excess.

The excess acid neutralises $20\text{ cm}^3$ of a solution of $0{,}1\text{ mol}\cdot\text{dm}^{-3}$ of magnesium hydroxide.

$2\text{HC}\ell(\text{aq}) + \text{Mg(OH)}_2(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{MgC}\ell_2(\text{aq}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\ell)$
question: Calculate the percentage purity of the sodium carbonate solution.
memo:
$n_{\text{Mg(OH)}_2} = (0{,}02)(0{,}1) \checkmark = 0{,}002\text{ mol}$
$n_{\text{HC}\ell(\text{excess})} = 2(0{,}002) = 0{,}004\text{ mol} \checkmark$
$n_{\text{HC}\ell(\text{react})} = 0{,}02 - 0{,}004 \checkmark = 0{,}016\text{ mol}$
$n_{\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3} = 0{,}008\text{ mol} \checkmark$
$m_{\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3} = nM = (0{,}008)(106) \checkmark = 0{,}848\text{ g} \checkmark$
$\text{Percentage purity} = \frac{0{,}848}{10} \times 100 \checkmark = 8{,}48\% \checkmark$
